text:
jamie_ae: Urgent - NovaSys POC hitting a flurry of 5xxs while ramping synthetic traffic. Demo livestream in 20m. They report ~110 rps sustained with spikes to 200. Need a short mitigation we can do without full infra changes.

omar_support: Any region/model and sample errors? Also any security or billing questions from them that might block changing configs?

jamie_ae: us-west-2, model=redwood-open-3b-q4-hosted. Error snippet from their harness: 
```
POST /v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{x-rw-queue-depth: 60, x-rw-backpressure: true}
{"error":"upstream overloaded","request_id":"req_nova_2026"}
```
They also asked about whether us-west data stays in-region (SQA note).

kelly_infra: Queue depth=60 + backpressure=true -> autoscaler didn't keep up and fallback coldstart lagging. Fast options: 
1) API-key scoped failover to smaller model (no infra spin): `redwoodctl api-keys update --id key-nova --set failover_model=redwood-open-1b-q4`
2) Temporarily set `min_replicas=1` for their 3B pool (costly but immediate warm replica)
3) Enable per-customer burstpool attach if allowed by policy.

chris_se: For the SQA question: us-west workloads are currently pinned to the us-west-2 hostpool for hosted customers; confirmable via contract. I'll DM legal for explicit wording if customer needs a clause.

omar_support: If we do failover, we can also set `failover_latency_threshold=500ms` so only slow requests route to 1B. That preserves quality for low-latency calls. Command: 
```
redwoodctl api-keys update --id key-nova --set failover_model=redwood-open-1b-q4 --set failover_latency_threshold=500ms
```

jamie_ae: AE asks about pricing impact if we bump min_replicas for the demo vs failover approach. Need a quick number to tell them.

kelly_infra: Back-of-envelope: min_replicas=1 for a 3B pool in us-west ~+$700/day; keeping it only for a 1-hour demo ~+$30. If we keep min_replicas=1 for full POC week, ~+$700/day * 7 = ~$4900 (subject to reserved discounts). Failover has near-zero infra delta for short-term spikes.

ops-bot: Alert: autoscaler-us-west-2 spike detected - queue_depth peaked at 64 for pool redwood-open-3b-q4 (alert id A-2026-11).

omar_support: While we push failover, grab logs: `curl -H "x-request-id: req_nova_2026" https://logs.internal/bundle` and `redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --since 30m --filter customer=novasys`. Also check pending_coldstarts.

jamie_ae: Flipped API key failover to 1B with threshold 500ms. Monitoring now.

chris_se: On the security/data residency front: send them an excerpt from our privacy page + assurance that logs are stored in the regional retention bucket; if they need a signed DPA addendum, escalate to legal. I'll start the request.

kelly_infra: After failover flip, error rates dropped significantly and demo proceeded. Follow-ups: 
- Add an AE pre-demo checklist: request prewarm window or allow failover toggle for demos.
- Investigate why burstpool auto-attach didn't trigger at queue_depth>50 (policy vs metrics mismatch).
- Consider a lightweight short-lifespan warm replica for scheduled demos to avoid coldstarts.

omar_support: I'll add a short KB article for AE/SE: "Quick fixes for demo ramps" with commands and cost bullets.

jamie_ae: Thanks team. NovaSys demo went live and demo flow preserved. Leaving ticket open for follow-up items (policy audit, KB, legal DPA). :rocket:
